```{julia}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
#| tags: [parameters]
source = "CFTP.qmd"

using EpidemicsCFTP, EpidemicsCFTP.abbreviations, EpidemicsUtilities
using DataFrames, PrettyTables
using Colors, Gadfly, Compose

import Test: @test
import Random: seed!
import Markdown
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
theme = create_theme(load_theme("config/test-theme.yml"))

set_default_plot_size(theme.figwidth, theme.figheight)
```

-----------------

Initialization
==============
Parameters are chosen simply to generate simple plots, and are not intended to be realistic!
The random `seed!` is chosen to deliver coalescence in first `12` iterations, but not too soon.
```{julia}
const population = 5 ; 
const duration   = 5.0 ;
const α          = 0.2 ;
const β          = 0.1 ;
seed!(7) ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
SEQUENCE=1:12
Markdown.parse("""
We will generate a short sequence of candidate innovations, starting with the minimal evolution,
and use these to generate successive `CEvolution`s over an algorithmic time sequence `$SEQUENCE`.
We use an expressive infix notation based on the "diamond" operator `⋄`, as in `ev = ev ⋄ iv`,
instead of
the clumsier (but equivalent) notation `ev = CEvolution(ev, iv)`.
""")
```
```{julia}
initial  = SIR(0.0, population - 1, 1, 0)

cremovals = C[C(t, population) for t ∈ [2,4]]

ev0_min = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, [z.t for z ∈ cremovals]; maximal=false) ;
ev0_max = extremal_evolution(initial, duration, [z.t for z ∈ cremovals]) ;

iv_null  = Innovation(initial.n, I[], R[], ev0_min.cremovals)
iv_seq   = [generate_innovation(iv_null, duration, α=α, β=β) for i ∈ SEQUENCE] ;
```


Tabular and graphical displays of epidemics
===========================================
`EpidemicsUtilities` supplies some constants 
used for the plotting parameter `select`, namely
```{julia}
import EpidemicsUtilities: ACTIVATED, BOUNDARIES, ELEMENTS, LFET, NFZ
```

To help set things up, we construct a prototype (_unconditioned_) `Evolution`.
```{julia}
reference = Evolution(initial, Innovation(initial.n, I[], [R(2t, t) for t ∈ [1,2]])).trajectory ;
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
uflow = table_trajectories1(duration, reference) ;
axes_plot = plot(uflow, yintercept=1:initial.n,
    Geom.hline(style=:dash, size=0.1mm, color=theme.scaffold),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration, ymin=0, ymax=initial.n + 0.25),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    style(default_color=theme.background),
    Theme(
        panel_fill=theme.blank,
        default_color=theme.default,
        background_color=theme.background,
        major_label_font="CMU Serif",   minor_label_font="CMU Serif",
        minor_label_color=theme.legend, major_label_color=theme.legend,
        major_label_font_size=8pt,     minor_label_font_size=6pt,
        grid_line_width=0mm,
)) ;

push!(axes_plot, layer(uflow, x=:t, y=:empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=2theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))) ;

lines_plot = new_figure(axes_plot,
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=(initial.n ≤ EpidemicsUtilities.MAXPOP ?
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_circled(i; n=initial.n) :
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_bracketed(i; n=initial.n))),
    Guide.yticks(ticks=collect(1:(initial.n))),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines")) ;
```

Here are colours to be used in CFTP plots.
```{julia}
min_spectrum   = [colorant"red"] ;
append!(min_spectrum, range(colorant"grey5",   stop=colorant"grey99", length=11)) ;
max_spectrum   = [colorant"green"] ;
append!(max_spectrum, range(colorant"grey5", stop=colorant"grey99",   length=11)) ;
joined_color   = colorant"gold" ;
coalesce_color = colorant"purple" ;
```

Algorithmic evolution from minimal (slowest) evolution
--------------------------------------------------

```{julia}
#| echo: false
Markdown.parse("""
We generate successive `CEvolution`s in algorithmic time, starting from minimal `CEvolution`.
@fig-CFTP-01-minstepA and 
@fig-CFTP-01-minstepB depict the first $(SEQUENCE[end]) algorithmic time steps.
Checks made on `LFE` and `NFZ`.
""")
```



```{julia}
ev, minimal = ev0_min, CEvolution[]
for iv ∈ iv_seq
    ev = ev ⋄ iv
    EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(ev) && EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_NFZ(ev)
    push!(minimal, ev)
end ;
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
for (i, ev) ∈ enumerate(minimal[SEQUENCE])
    depict("CFTP-01-minstep$i", new_figure(
        draw_evolution!(deepcopy(lines_plot), ev, duration, theme=theme,
                select=BOUNDARIES | ELEMENTS | ACTIVATED | LFET | NFZ),
            title="Min evolution, step $i")
        ) ;
end
```


Algorithmic evolution from maximal (fastest) evolution
--------------------------------------------------
```{julia}

and @fig-CFTP-02-maxstepB depict the first 
$(SEQUENCE[end]) algorithmic time steps.
Checks made an `LFE` and `NFZ` again.
""")
```

```{julia}
ev, maximal = ev0_max, CEvolution[]
for iv ∈ iv_seq  
    ev = ev ⋄ iv
    EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(ev) && EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_NFZ(ev)
    push!(maximal, ev)
end ;
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
for (i, ev) ∈ enumerate(maximal[SEQUENCE])
```

Comparison of minimal and maximal sequences
-------------------------------------------
```{julia}
#| echo: false
Markdown.parse("""
Finally we compare minimal (red) with maximal (green)
epidemic trajectories.
Fully coalesced trajectories are coloured purple.
To be specific, @fig-CFTP-03-stepA plots both minimal and maximal evolutions
for the first six steps in algorithmic time. 
@fig-CFTP-03-stepB plots the remaining steps. 

Monotonicity is checked and is
$(all(minimal .⪯ maximal) ? "**maintained** throughout" : "**not** maintained"),
while full coalescence (_including_ agreement of `CRemoval` `target` fields) occurs at 
algorithmic time step $(findfirst(minimal .≃ maximal)) 
$(all((minimal .≃ maximal)[findfirst(minimal .≃ maximal):end]) ? "and then **persists**" : "but does **not** persist").
(Note that the _trajectories_ coincide at an earlier stage of algorithmic time,
namely step 3: 
however at this point the
`CRemoval` `target` fields do not agree, so later trajectories are able to diverge.)
""")
```
```{julia}
@test all(minimal .⪯ maximal) ;                                      # monotonicity
@test all((minimal .≃ maximal)[findfirst(minimal .≃ maximal):end]) ; # persistence
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
for k ∈ SEQUENCE
    print(rpad("Step $k: ", 15),    sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), minimal[k].cremovals))
    println(rpad(minimal[k] ≃ maximal[k] ? "  coalesced with" : "", 18), 
                                    sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), maximal[k].cremovals))
end
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false   
for k ∈ SEQUENCE
    work = deepcopy(lines_plot)
    if minimal[k] ≃ maximal[k]
        draw_evolution!(work, maximal[k], duration, theme=theme,
                        select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=coalesce_color)
    end
    draw_evolution!(work, minimal[k], duration, theme=theme, 
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=min_spectrum[1])
    draw_evolution!(work, maximal[k], duration, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=max_spectrum[1])
    depict("CFTP-03-step$k", new_figure(work, title="Evolution at step $k"))
end ;
```

Detailed graphical study of coalescence
---------------------------------------
```{julia}
#| echo: false
Markdown.parse("""
For the purposes of understanding CFTP we need also to look at behaviours of maximal (green) 
and minimal (blue)
epidemic trajectories started at algorithmic times in the range $(2:(SEQUENCE[end-1])).
These are plotted using colour-coding: later starts have different colours.
Again at full coalescence of the earliest start, the common trajectory is plotted in purple.
Before full coalescence, the initial part of the common to both maximal and minimal earliest
starts is coloured gold.
Note that the coalesced trajectory captures earlier starts quite fast ...
""")
```

```{julia}
minimal_tally = Dict()
for start_time ∈ SEQUENCE
    ev = ev0_min
    minimal_tally[start_time] = []
    for (index, iv) ∈ enumerate(iv_seq[start_time:end])
        ev_old = deepcopy(ev)
        try
            ev = ev ⋄ iv
            EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(ev) && EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_NFZ(ev)
        catch e
            if (e isa ExpungedInfectionGivesValidTrajectory) || (e isa MissedCRemoval)
                println("MINIMAL $start_time:$index")
                println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), e))
                println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev_old))
                println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), iv))
                println()
                println(e)
                println(ev_old)
                println(iv)
            end
            rethrow()
        end
        push!(minimal_tally[start_time], ev)
    end
end


maximal_tally = Dict()
for start_time ∈ SEQUENCE
    ev = ev0_max
    maximal_tally[start_time] = []
    for (index, iv) ∈ enumerate(iv_seq[start_time:end])
        ev_old = deepcopy(ev)
        try
            ev = ev ⋄ iv
            EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_LFE(ev) && EpidemicsCFTP.is_correct_NFZ(ev)
        catch e
            if e isa ExpungedInfectionGivesValidTrajectory || e isa MissedCRemoval
                println("MAXIMAL $start_time:$index")
                println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), e))
                println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), ev_old))
                println(sprint(show, MIME("text/plain"), iv))
                println()
                println(e)
                println(ev_old)
                println(iv)
            end
            rethrow()
        end
        push!(maximal_tally[start_time], ev)
    end
end
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false   
for k ∈ SEQUENCE
    work = deepcopy(lines_plot)
    if minimal[k] ≃ maximal[k]
        draw_evolution!(work, maximal[k], duration, theme=theme,
                        select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=coalesce_color)
    end
    
    paired = collect(zip(minimal[k].trajectory, maximal[k].trajectory))
    ex = findfirst(z -> !==(z[1], z[2]), paired)
    if isnothing(ex)
        draw_evolution!(work, maximal[k], duration, theme=theme, 
                        select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=joined_color)
    elseif ex > 1
        conjoined = maximal[k].trajectory[1:(ex-1)]
        mn, mx = minimal[k].trajectory[ex-1], maximal[k].trajectory[ex]
        push!(conjoined, SIR(mx.t, mn.s, mn.i, mn.r))
        df = table_trajectories1(conjoined[end].t, conjoined)
        push!(work, layer(df, x=:t, y=:epidemic, Geom.step,
                         style(line_width=theme.boundary, 
                         default_color=joined_color)))
    end
    
    # Now draw the relevant minimal and maximal starts at times later than the initial time.
    for r ∈ 1:k
        draw_evolution!(work, minimal_tally[r][k-r+1], duration, theme=theme, 
                        select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=min_spectrum[r])
    end
    for r ∈ 1:k
        draw_evolution!(work, maximal_tally[r][k-r+1], duration, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=max_spectrum[r])

    # Finally display the figure
    depict("CFTP-04-comb$k", new_figure(work, title="CFTP at step $k"))
    end
end ;
```

Here is an experimental check of monotonicity between starts at different time ("sandwiching").
```{julia}
for start_time ∈ SEQUENCE[2:end]
    for s ∈ 1:(SEQUENCE[end] - start_time + 1)
        @test maximal_tally[start_time - 1][s+1] ⪯ maximal_tally[start_time][s]
        @test minimal_tally[start_time][s] ⪯ minimal_tally[start_time - 1][s+1]
    end
end ;
```

Creation of a unit test
=======================
We select one of the sequences `minimal` and `maximal` driven by `iv_seq`,
and one particular `index > 1`.
```{julia}
ev_seq = minimal
index = 8
ev1 = ev_seq[index - 1]
iv2 = iv_seq[index]
ev2 = ev_seq[index] ;
```

Now the act of updating a `CEvolution` is actually invariant under monotonic transformation
of the time axis. Thus we can replace the set of all times arising
in either of `ev1`, `iv2` (and therefore, by construction, `ev2`), by their integer ranks,
so producing discretized versions `dev1`, `div2` and `dev2`:
```{julia}
compendium = sort([z.t for z in ev1.chronology ∪ iv2.infections ∪ iv2.removals])
rank_time = Dict()
rank_time[ Inf] =  Inf
rank_time[-Inf] = -Inf
@test allunique(compendium)
for (r, t) in enumerate(compendium)
    rank_time[t] = r
end

function rank_incident(z::AbstractInfection)
    return typeof(z)(rank_time[z.t], z.target, z.infectee)
end
function rank_incident(z::AbstractRemoval)
    return typeof(z)(rank_time[z.t], z.target)
end
dev1 = CEvolution(ev1.initial, [rank_incident(z) for z in ev1.chronology])
div2 = Innovation(iv2.population, [rank_incident(z) for z in iv2.chronology])
dev2 = CEvolution(ev2.initial, [rank_incident(z) for z in ev2.chronology],
    LFE=[rank_incident(z) for z in ev2.LFE], NFZ=[rank_time[t] for t in ev2.NFZ]) ;
```
Note there will be no need to fill the `LFE` and `NFZ` fields for `dev1`.

Now update `dev1` using `dev2` to produce `ddev2`:
```{julia}
ddev2 = dev1 ⋄ div2 ;
```
Then `ddev2` is the same as `dev2`:
```{julia}
@test dev2.chronology == ddev2.chronology ;
@test dev2.LFE == ddev2.LFE ;
@test dev2.NFZ == ddev2.NFZ ;
```

So we can print off `dev1`, `iv2` and dev2` to produce the data for a unit test.

```{julia}
unit_test_string = """

# Produced from `CFTP.qmd` at index=$index, maximal
@testset "EpidemicsCFTP: $(rpad("Testing one-step ()", 23))" begin
    initial = $(dev1.initial)

    dev1 = CEvolution(initial,
        $(sprint(show, dev1.chronology))
        )

    div2 = Innovation($(div2.population),
        $(sprint(show, div2.infections)),
        $(sprint(show, div2.removals)),
        $(sprint(show, div2.cremovals))
        )

    dev2 = CEvolution(initial,
        $(sprint(show, dev2.chronology));
        LFE=$(sprint(show, dev2.LFE)),
        NFZ=$(sprint(show, dev2.NFZ))
        )

    ddev2 = dev1 ⋄ div2

    @test dev2.infections == ddev2.infections
    @test dev2.removals   == ddev2.removals
    @test dev2.cremovals  == ddev2.cremovals
    @test dev2.LFE        == ddev2.LFE
    @test dev2.NFZ        == ddev2.NFZ
end

"""

unit_test_string = replace(unit_test_string,
    "AbstractIncident"   => "AI",
    "AbstractInfection"  => "AIF",
    "PInfection"         => "P",
    "NoFlyInfection"     => "NF",
    "ExpungedInfection"  => "XI",
    "KilledInfection"    => "KI",
    "Infection"          => "I",

    "AbstractRemoval"    => "AIR",
    "KilledRemoval"      => "KR",
    "CRemoval"           => "C",
    "Removal"            => "R",

    ".0"                 => "",
    ", "                 => ",",
    )

open("CFTP-unit.txt", "w") do file
    write(file, unit_test_string)
end
```

{{< pagebreak >}}


A longer example
================
Here is an example from @ONeillRoberts-1999. Removals are observed with the following 
interremoval times (adjusted to avoid coincidences):
```{julia}
interremovals = 
    [13, 7,   2, 3,   0.1, 0.1, 1,   4, 5,   3,
      2, 0.1, 2, 0.1, 5,   3,   1,   4, 0.1, 1,
      1, 1,   2, 0.1, 1,   5,   0.1, 5, 5]
size = length(interremovals) + 1 ;
```
We compute actual times of removals, assuming initial removal takes place `10` days after infection
(this is an arbitrary choice, and perhaps CFTP needs to be extended to deal with uncertainty about number of initial infectives?).
Also we assume the first observed removal to happen at time zero,
```{julia}
cremoval_times = accumulate(+,interremovals, init=0) ;
```
we assume a good Bayesian justification for a prior distribution of numbers of infectives at this time!

We create maximal and minimal initial evolutions. Here `duration` is extended to `10` days after final removal,
which is primarily a photogenic choice.
```{julia}
pop = 120
initial   = SIR(0, pop-1, 1, 0)
duration2 = 10 + maximum(cremoval_times)
α0=0.0008
β0=0.08
evmin = extremal_evolution(initial, duration2, cremoval_times, 
    maximal=false) ;
evmax = extremal_evolution(initial, duration2, cremoval_times, 
    maximal=true, all_cremovals_observed=true) ;
```

Revised colours.
```{julia}
min_spectrum   = [colorant"red"] ;
append!(min_spectrum, range(colorant"grey5",   stop=colorant"grey99", length=11)) ;
max_spectrum   = [colorant"blue"] ;
append!(max_spectrum, range(colorant"grey5", stop=colorant"grey99",   length=11)) ;
joined_color   = colorant"gold" ;
coalesce_color = colorant"purple" ;
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
set_default_plot_size(2theme.figwidth, 0.8theme.figheight)
ylines = 0:5:size

uflow = table_trajectories1(duration2, evmin.trajectory) ;
axes_plot2 = plot(uflow, 
    yintercept=ylines,
    Geom.hline(style=:dash, size=0.1mm, color=theme.scaffold),
    Coord.cartesian(xmin=0, xmax=duration2, ymin=0, ymax=size + 0.25),
    Guide.xlabel("Process time", orientation=:horizontal),
    style(default_color=theme.background),
    Theme(
        panel_fill=theme.blank,
        default_color=theme.default,
        background_color=theme.background,
        major_label_font="CMU Serif",   minor_label_font="CMU Serif",
        minor_label_color=theme.legend, major_label_color=theme.legend,
        major_label_font_size=6pt,     minor_label_font_size=4pt,
        plot_padding = [4pt, 2pt, 4pt, 4pt],
        grid_line_width=0mm,
)) ;

push!(axes_plot2, layer(uflow, x=:t, y=:empty, Geom.line,
    style(line_width=theme.trail, default_color=theme.scaffold))) ;

lines_plot2 = new_figure(axes_plot2,
    Scale.y_continuous(labels=(initial.n ≤ EpidemicsUtilities.MAXPOP ?
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_circled(i; n=initial.n) :
        i -> EpidemicsUtilities.timelinelabels_bracketed(i; n=initial.n))),
    Guide.yticks(ticks=ylines),
    Guide.ylabel("Time lines")) ;
```


A function `repetition_and_display` uses the template `Innovation` `iv_null`
and updates minimal and maximal `CEvolution`s by a specified number of algorithmic steps.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
import Distributions
min_cremovals = [CRemoval(t, n) for (n, t) in enumerate(cremoval_times)]
iv_null  = Innovation(initial.n, Infection[], Removal[], min_cremovals) ;
@test size == length(min_cremovals) + 1
function repetition_and_display(evmin, evmax, n; duration2=duration2, iv_null=iv_null,
                    α0=α0, β0=β0, lines_plot2=lines_plot2)
    for i in 1:n
        iv    = generate_innovation(iv_null, duration2; α=α0, β=β0, size=size) ;
        evmin = evmin ⋄ iv ;
        evmax = evmax ⋄ iv ;
        
        # Start of proposal to check a new initial condition.
        # IRL we'd use a distribution with Bayesian justification!
        proposed_start = rand(Distributions.DiscreteUniform(evmin.initial.r + 1, size))
        
        new_initial = SIR(evmin.initial.t, 
            evmin.initial.n - proposed_start, proposed_start - evmin.initial.r, evmin.initial.r)
        try
            new_evmin = CEvolution(new_initial, evmin.chronology)
            evmin = new_evmin
        catch e
            if !((e isa EmployedRemoval) || (e isa MissedCRemoval))
                rethrow()
            end
        end
        
        new_initial = SIR(evmax.initial.t, 
            evmax.initial.n - proposed_start, proposed_start - evmax.initial.r, evmax.initial.r)
        try
            new_evmax = CEvolution(new_initial, evmax.chronology)
            evmax = new_evmax
        catch e
            if !((e isa EmployedRemoval) || (e isa MissedCRemoval))
                rethrow()
            end
        end
        # End of proposal to check a new initial condition.
        
    end
    slogan = (evmin ≃ evmax) ? " [COALESCENCE]" : ""
    work = deepcopy(lines_plot2)
    draw_evolution!(work, evmin, duration2, theme=theme, 
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=min_spectrum[1])
    draw_evolution!(work, evmax, duration2, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=max_spectrum[1])
    return work, evmin, evmax, slogan
end ;
```
We use this to plot a sequence of updates in algorithmic time.
```{julia}
#| echo: false
iteration = 0
slogan    = ""
work = deepcopy(lines_plot2)
draw_evolution!(work, evmin, duration2, theme=theme, 
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=min_spectrum[1])
draw_evolution!(work, evmax, duration2, theme=theme,
                    select=BOUNDARIES, specified_color=max_spectrum[1])
depict("", new_figure(work, title="Minimum and maximum evolutions at algorithmic time step $iteration $slogan"))
```

```{julia}
#| echo: false
iteration0 = iteration
iteration  = 1
(work, evmin, evmax, slogan) = repetition_and_display(evmin, evmax, iteration-iteration0)
depict("", new_figure(work, title="Minimum and maximum evolutions at algorithmic time step $iteration $slogan"))
```
